name: Renfield Shake Motor
description:
12V shake motor - 'the signature', Renfield's tremble. Cytron MDD (MDD10A-class, DIR+PWM per channel) on channel 1. BCM GPIO: DIR1=26, PWM1=13.

This MATCHES fleet convention - GPIO 13 is the PWM line on every MDD10A in MonsterBox, and PumpkinHead uses the identical pair (DIR=26, PWM=13). The pins were briefly wired the other way round on 2026-09-13 and the operator swapped them back the same day; if you find a note anywhere claiming Renfield is reversed, it is stale. DIR and PWM are still not interchangeable: swapped, motor_control.py puts the 2kHz PWM train on the DIR line and a static level on the PWM line, so the board sees a permanently-asserted enable with direction chattering - the motor runs flat out and speed does nothing.

TWO-PIN BOARD - do not re-add rpwmPin/lpwmPin/renPin/lenPin. This part was specced for a BTS7960 and never built; the driver changed at the bench. services/hardwareService/index.js dispatches on controlBoard === 'BTS7960' && rpwmPin != null && lpwmPin != null, and killInFlightDrive() tests rpwmPin BEFORE directionPin - so stale four-pin keys send both the drive and the stop down the BTS7960 path, against pins this board does not have, while still reporting success.

POWER: 12V PSU -> slow-blow fuse -> NTC inrush limiter (5-10 ohm) -> B+. 10,000uF/25V+ across B+/B- at the board, stripe to B-; without the NTC that cap is a dead short at power-on and trips the PSU's OCP. RC snubber (0.1uF film + 10-47 ohm 1W) across the MOTOR terminals at the motor - a bare cap with no series resistor shorts the H-bridge on every PWM edge and cooks the MOSFETs. Star ground at B-; Pi GND runs to the control header GND only, carrying signal return, never motor current. The 12V motor supply must NOT share the Pi's 5V rail.

PULL-DOWNS: 10k from DIR and PWM to GND at the driver end. scripts/motor_control.py calls gpio_free() on both pins when a run ends and a Pi reboot returns them to input, so both float otherwise - on a yard prop that reads as the motor running when nobody is home.

STALL: a wiper-class motor stalls at roughly 24-40A, above the MDD10A's 30A peak. Short bursts only - scenes run 900-2000ms at 50-80% and maxDuration caps any single energization at 5000ms. Groundbreaker's wiper motor stalled mid-test 2026-08-30 and its 12V rail is still dead; a stalled motor cooks until the fuse opens, and PWM outlives the process.

HISTORY 2026-09-26: this MDD shape was first committed 2026-09-13 (3b32a1ec) but never reached the node; the 2026-09-20 lock pulled the node's stale BTS7960 copy (rpwmPin 12 / lpwmPin 13, enabled:false) back into the repo and froze it, so the first bench test after wiring drove GPIO 12/13 down the BTS7960 path and the motor stayed still. Operator confirmed the wiring 2026-09-26; part restored, enabled, and its physical-faults entry cleared.

name: Speaker Renfield (ReSpeaker XVF3800)
description: powered speakers on the ReSpeaker XVF3800 line-out (the Pi 5 has no analog jack, so this is the only non-HDMI output). OPERATOR 2026-08-31: these are a good set of powered speakers, the SAME set as Sir Dragomir (character 4) uses - his speaker part carries the same modelId speaker_respeaker_xvf3800. Treat his tuning as the nearest reference point for Renfield.

name: Renfield Eye Rings
description:
Two chained DIYMall X0040MB5LN 8-bit WS2812B rings on GPIO18 - left eye pixels 0-7, right eye 8-15. Same hardware and same wiring as PumpkinHead's Pumpkin Eyes.

This part was registered as a plain switched `light` until 2026-09-20, which is why Renfield could toggle his eyes on and off and had no speech sync, no AI interaction colours and nothing on /setup/led-animation: every one of those paths selects parts by `type === 'led_ring'` and a `light` is invisible to all of them.

The old description claimed the rings were NOT addressable because rpi_ws281x cannot drive pixels on a Pi 5. The premise was right and the conclusion was wrong: rpi_ws281x fails because RP1 moved GPIO off the SoC, but RP1's own PIO block clocks WS2812B fine and needs no root (/dev/pio0 is root:gpio, and the service user is in the gpio group). led_ring_daemon.py picks that backend automatically on a Pi 5. Measured here: 500 frames at a steady 50 Hz with flat RSS.

GPIO18 is free on this node - the motor holds 12 and 13. It is also the Pi's I2S PCM_CLK line, unused because Renfield's audio is entirely USB (ReSpeaker XVF3800); move these rings first if I2S is ever enabled here. The PWM0/snd_bcm2835 contention that matters on a Pi 4 does not apply on this board, because the PIO path never touches PWM0.

name: PIR Motion Sensor
description: PIR motion sensor on BCM GPIO 22 (operator-stated wiring, 2026-09-26; first recorded as GPIO 16 the same evening, corrected by the operator). Output goes HIGH on motion; read with an internal pull-down (lgpio on this Pi 5 — no /dev/gpiomem). Arms the Motion toggle: detection -> AI + eye rings + shake + pen.

name: Writing Pen
description: Miuzei MG90S 180-degree micro servo that moves Renfield's writing pen. Driven DIRECTLY from BCM GPIO 26 (operator-stated wiring, 2026-09-26) with lgpio tx_servo through servo_cli.py move_to — there is no PCA9685 on this Pi 5. Pulse 500-2400 us, 50 Hz. Servo power must come from a 5-6 V rail with a common ground to the Pi, never the Pi's 3.3 V. WIRING CONFLICT TO RESOLVE: the shake motor (part 1) was recorded on DIR=26 / PWM=13 on 2026-09-13; the pen now owns GPIO 26, so the motor's DIR line must be on another pin — confirm with the operator and update part 1. Not yet calibrated: run Set Min/Max on /setup/calibration so the pen's real travel is measured before scenes push it to its ends.
